items.stem: A language model is given "The capital of France is" and shows Paris with a probability of 0.89. What does the 0.89 mean?

options.text: If it picks at random in proportion to these numbers, it chooses Paris about 89 times in 100.
options.feedback: A probability says how likely the model is to pick that word. It comes from patterns in the training text.

options.text: The model checked a list of capital cities and is 89 percent sure that Paris is correct.
options.feedback: The model has no fact lookup step. The 0.89 comes from how often sentences that begin this way ended with Paris in the training text.

options.text: Paris appears in 89 percent of all the sentences in the training text.
options.feedback: The number describes what usually follows this particular start of a sentence. It does not describe how often Paris appears overall.

options.text: The model's answer is 89 percent likely to be factually correct.
options.feedback: The number says how likely the word is to be picked. It does not say whether the answer is true, and a wrong word can also have a high probability.

items.stem: You ask a model the same question ten times at temperature 0. What do you expect to see?

options.feedback: At temperature 0 the model always takes the top word, so the same prompt gives the same answer.
Different answers need some randomness, which comes from a temperature above 0.
The answer is the same each time, but it is correct only if the most likely word happens to be correct.

options.text: Mostly the same answer, with one or two variations
options.feedback: At temperature 0 there is no random choice, so there are no variations.

items.stem: A company sets the temperature of its chatbot to 0 so that it gives the same answer every time. A customer asks a question, and the most likely word at one point is wrong. What happens?

options.text: The chatbot gives the same wrong answer every time the question is asked.
options.feedback: Temperature 0 always takes the most likely word. If that word is wrong, the error repeats in the same words every time.

options.text: The chatbot notices the low reliability and corrects itself.
options.feedback: There is no checking step. The model picks a word and moves on.

options.text: The chatbot varies its answer, so some of the answers will be right.
options.feedback: Varying the answer needs a temperature above 0. At 0 the answer never varies.

options.text: The chatbot refuses to answer, because it is unsure.
options.feedback: The model has no step that decides to refuse based on its probabilities. It writes whatever the top word leads to.

items.stem: A model is writing a long answer, and its third word is slightly wrong. What is most likely to happen to the rest of the answer?

options.text: Later words are chosen to fit the wrong word, so the error carries forward.
options.feedback: Each word is chosen as a likely continuation of the text so far, and that text now includes the wrong word.

options.text: The model notices the problem at the end and goes back to fix the third word.
options.feedback: The model never goes back. Each word is added to the end and stays there.

options.text: The rest of the answer is unaffected, because each word is chosen on its own.
options.feedback: Each word is chosen with all the earlier words in the prompt, so an early error shapes everything after it.

options.text: The model stops at the wrong word and reports an error to the user.
options.feedback: Nothing in the process detects a wrong word, so no error is reported.
